What Coquette AI Is

Coquette AI, also written Coquette, is a web companion for fictional adult chat. The terms describe AI companions as automated systems with no consciousness, emotions, or real-world agency.

The same clause says the service is entertainment, not medical, psychological, legal, or financial advice. Replies can be inaccurate, and you are responsible for how you use them.

The terms say you must be at least 18, and that using the site is your warranty of that. They do not describe an identity document or a selfie check.

The homepage we opened the same day was a grid of named cards, not a pricing table. In the text captured from that view we counted 80 names.

Some cards printed an age and some did not. Where an age was printed, the figures we saw were 18, 19, 20, 21, 24, 25, 26, 30, 38, 45, and 46.

The lowest printed age in that capture was 18. A missing age on a card is not the same thing as a stated adult age.

Several cards in that capture are written as step-family roleplay. The terms we read do not add a separate ban on that theme.

That is a content-policy difference from companions that forbid step-family roleplay in writing. It is not a reason to treat a printed 18 as a document check.

The terms also say the company may change, pause, or remove any part of the service without notice. A catalog count from one afternoon can move.

Chat and What We Could Not Price

Messaging and the free cap

Paid plans include unlimited messaging. The terms say free access exists, and that its limits are set by the company.

Neither the terms nor the Premium page text we captured printed that free number. We did not create an account, so we did not watch a counter hit zero.

A subscription also includes a monthly allocation of tokens, "as disclosed at checkout." The Premium page text we captured did not print a token count.

Independent write-ups have quoted a round number. We are not repeating it as a verified figure.

If the job is explicit back-and-forth more than a card grid, SpicyRanked's best AI sexting apps is the wider shelf.

Characters you build

The terms have a section on user-created companions. Anything you create or customize through the platform remains the company's property.

You get a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable, non-commercial license to use that content inside the platform. No commercial rights are granted.

We did not open a builder, so we did not see whether a photo upload, an age field, or a style picker is on the screen. The property clause does not depend on that screen.

If you leave, the license is already described as revocable. Do not assume a character you shaped is a file you can take with you.

Photos, voice, and video

The terms say tokens pay for certain features, and that tokens have no cash value. They do not price a still, a voice note, or a clip.

The Premium page text we captured talked about unlimited access, a sale, and cancel-anytime. It did not itemize photos, calls, or video.

We are not going to invent those rates. Read the generator, if one is on your account, before you spend the month's tokens.

Plan Prices

The Premium page is public. On 28 November 2026 it showed a spring-sale banner for new users, and it said "100% anonymous" and "You can cancel anytime."

Sale styling can make a struck-through number look like the price. Read the checkout, not only the tile.

We did not pay, so the statement descriptor is unverified. "100% anonymous" is the page's claim, not a line we saw on a bank statement.

The terms say a subscription renews automatically unless you cancel before the renewal. Payment is taken at the start of each new billing period.

You are responsible for fees and taxes. The company says it is not liable for problems that come from an unauthorized third-party checkout.

What tokens do, and what they do not

Tokens are personal and non-transferable. They cannot be exchanged for cash, and they are not a substitute for payment.

They expire at the end of the billing period. They do not roll over.

When a paid plan ends, unused tokens expire and cannot be restored. A refund, if one is granted, cancels the paid service immediately and revokes the tokens that remain.

That is a hard shape. A yearly bill of $46.79 does not build a token balance you can sit on.

Cancel and refunds

You cancel in account settings. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the current period, and the account then returns to the free version.

Premium features stop at that point. The terms do not describe an app-store subscription, so we are not describing an App Store or Google Play cancel path.

Refund requests for a subscription must be submitted within 24 hours of payment. No refund is granted if more than 20 tokens have been used.

Only credit-card payments are eligible under that clause. Token-pack refunds, if you buy a pack, also have to be requested within 24 hours, and they are refused once any of those tokens are used.

The terms say extra statutory rights may apply in the EU or the UK. They also say repeated refunds, extra accounts used to get refunds, or a chargeback can end the account.

You are told to contact the company before a chargeback. A chargeback can suspend access and wipe remaining tokens.

Legal mail is legal@coquette.ai. General contact on the pages we opened is contact@coquette.ai.

Those addresses are text, not a promise that a reply arrives inside the 24-hour refund window. Write before you spend the tokens if you might want the money back.

Safety Rules

The eligibility line is 18, with legal capacity to contract. We did not see a named age-check vendor in the terms.

The prohibited-uses section bans unlawful, abusive, harmful, fraudulent, or exploitative use. The examples are harassment or exploitation, distributing illegal content, reverse engineering, getting around payment limits, and opening extra accounts to abuse promotions or refunds.

Illegal content covers a great deal of law, including anything sexual involving a minor. The list we read does not spell out a separate ban on characters who look underage, on real-person likenesses, or on deepfakes.

We did not submit a banned prompt, so enforcement is unread. A short list is not the same thing as a tested filter.

The content-moderation clause says the company may remove material that breaks the terms or the law. It does not publish a response time.

The terms and privacy pages we opened do not include a 2257 statement. We are not saying none exists elsewhere on the site.

We are saying it was not in the two legal documents this review relies on. If a record-keeping page matters to you, find it before you pay.

User content you generate stays the company's property under the license above. That is an ownership rule, not a safety filter, and it still belongs next to the safety read.

Privacy Rules

The privacy policy names Euranka Sarl as the controller for personal data on the service. It cites the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection and the GDPR for users in the EEA.

The terms, updated later, define "Company" as Coquette.ai. They put disputes under Swiss law and the courts of Lausanne, and they do not print a street address or a company number.

A controller name in one document and a product name in the other is a real gap. We did not match a registration number on the Coquette pages we opened, so this review does not quote one.

The privacy policy says the service does not sell or rent personal data. It may share data with providers for hosting, analytics, and payments, with authorities when the law requires it, and with a buyer if the business is sold.

Account data is kept while the account is active. Payment and transaction records can be kept for up to 7 years.

Conversations and AI interactions are stored for a limited period to improve the service, and then anonymized. The policy does not define that period in days.

Data collected includes name, email, username, and an encrypted password, plus chats, preferences, billing status, IP address, browser, device, and messages you send to support. Card numbers are described as handled by payment providers, not as a number the policy says Coquette stores itself.

If data leaves Switzerland or the EEA, the policy points to standard contractual clauses or Swiss law. Your listed rights, for EEA or Swiss residents, include access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability, objection, and withdrawing consent.

The policy text we captured was cut off in the rights section before a contact address for those requests. Use legal@coquette.ai if the live page does not name another inbox, and keep a copy.

Leaving a companion app in general is in our guide to deleting AI companion data. SpicyRanked's how to delete AI companion data lists the same order for a longer set of apps.

What to read before you type a scene you would not want reused is in AI adult tools and your data. On Coquette, the improve-the-service line is the clause to read twice.

Anonymized later is not the same as never stored. The privacy policy is from February 2025, and the terms are from February 2026, so the newer document is the terms.

Coquette Verdict

Coquette AI publishes a Premium price before you create an account, and the privacy policy names Euranka Sarl. The yearly bill on the page we opened was $46.79.

Unlimited messaging, if the checkout matches the terms, is simpler than a coin on every reply. Tokens still expire, and they still do not roll over.

The free cap and the monthly token count were not on the public pages we used. Photo, voice, and video prices were not either.

The refund window is 24 hours, and it dies after 20 tokens. The terms do not print a company number, and the prohibited-use list is short.

Chats are stored to improve the service and then anonymized. Characters you build remain the company's property.

We score Coquette AI 6.4 out of 10, conditional. Read the checkout for the token grant.
